Definition: adverb from G1537; out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively:--away, forth, (with-)out (of, -ward), strange.
BiblicalUsage: éxō is the word for outside, without. In Matthew 5:13, the text says "but to be cast out." In Mark 1:45, the text says "But he went out."
TheologicalSignificance: What éxō teaches me is that God's judgment is just, and it falls where it should — no one escapes it, and no one suffers it unjustly. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; The Sermon on the Mount; The Birth of John the Baptist
